figures.shows: Taxonomy diagram: AI models, quantum computers and quantum simulators feed three tasks: linear properties Tr(rho O) (local: correlation, magnetization; global: order parameters, direct fidelity estimation), nonlinear properties (entanglement and stabilizer entropy, purity, mutual information, phase classification), and reconstructing quantum systems (implicit state reconstruction, Q_theta approximates P with P(i) = Tr(rho |i><i|)); each task has icons for ML, DL and LM; applications: quantum algorithm enhancement, certification and benchmarks, scientific discovery.
figures.confirmed_by: Representing and characterizing ground states generated by quantum analog simulators and quantum states produced by digital quantum computers can be classified into three major tasks: predicting linear properties, predicting nonlinear properties, and reconstructing quantum states and processes.

figures.shows: Nested hierarchy: artificial intelligence (logic-based) contains machine learning models (kernel methods, regression models, tree-based models), which contain deep learning models (FCNN/CNN, GNN, RNN/LSTM/PixelCNNs), which contain language models (GPT-based methods).
figures.confirmed_by: The hierarchy reflects the increasing capability of AI models and their growing adaptability to handle large-scale quantum systems, progressing from the broad concept of AI to machine learning models, deep learning models, and transformer-based models.

assertions.value: The authors use the one-dimensional transverse-field Ising model with periodic boundary condition, set h = J = 1, so the system is at its critical field hc = J, gapless in the thermodynamic limit, with a highly entangled critical ground state.

assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own measurement setup (Section II.A, p.2).
